claims.text: An optimal degree of short-range chemical order promotes a cooperative second-order magnetic transition in rare-earth-free NiFeCoCr-based HEAs.
Short-range chemical order enhances the magnetocaloric effect at low applied fields.
The proposed ordering state preserves rapid heat exchange and robust mechanical properties.
The as-cast, near-equiatomic NiFeCoCr-based baseline has a largely random chemical distribution.
Post-casting annealing and controlled cooling can tune the degree of short-range chemical order.
The magnetic transition temperature of NiFeCoCr-based alloys can occur near or above room temperature.
Increasing short-range chemical order produces greater local magnetic homogeneity.
Annealing induces partial chemical ordering in the alloy.
Heat treatment narrows the distribution of local exchange interactions in NiFeCoCr-based alloys.
A narrower distribution of exchange interactions creates a smoother, cooperative second-order magnetic transition.
The smoother second-order transition maximizes magnetic entropy change at low fields.
The second-order transition avoids abrupt structural discontinuities.
Avoiding abrupt structural discontinuities prevents degradation of heat transfer and mechanical integrity.
An intermediate annealing condition will enhance the magnetocaloric response by approximately 20–30% over the as-cast baseline.
The optimum annealing condition will reduce magnetic hysteresis relative to the as-cast baseline.
The optimum annealing condition will preserve or improve mechanical strength.
The optimum annealing condition will preserve thermal conductivity or heat-transfer rate.
As-cast samples have lower magnetic entropy change and require higher fields for an effective magnetocaloric response.
The hypothesis extends to similar near-equiatomic transition-metal HEAs with either single-phase or dual-phase structures.
Large changes in composition, phase constitution, or atomic-size mismatch fall outside the proposed regime.
